a true random number generator with provable security and built-in resilience against adversarial attacks can be implemented in a small number of oscillators.

(1) the fill rate is the right measure of randomness for the output of an oscillator-ring based true random number generator, (2) the fill rate decreases exponentially with the number of oscillating elements, (3) resilient functions can be used to extract random bits from signals with low fill rates and, (4) resilient functions can also be used to withstand fault attacks.
the proposed design (1) generates provably random bits, (2) is secure against a large class of attacks, and (3) can be implemented with a few tens of oscillators and a few kilobytes of memory.
